$comment: Where things happened. A place is not a floor: floors are the spine and live in books.json, while a place is somewhere on one — a city, a castle, a district, a dimension. They earn an entry when the crawl keeps coming back to them or when a beat elsewhere needs somewhere to point.

tagline.text: A name on a guarded casino stairwell, with cheering coming up it. The capital of the disputed lands, says a crocodilian guard, and the prize the factions fight over.
The capital of the disputed lands, the big city on the ninth floor. The factions camped around it are forbidden to fight over it until crawlers arrive.
The City of Dreams at the centre of the pie, a castle at the heart of it, and thirty days for nine armies to settle who holds it.
Drained down to its bottom three rings, the castle still under water, and the System's welcome still calls it the City of Dreams.

beats.headline: A city named on the surface
beats.text: Carl and Donut come up out of the water with the concierge sharks behind them and once they reach a town that will take them in, Katia reads the Mad Dune Mage's page of numbers as places the Gate can open onto, every one of them around Larracos, the capital city four floors below them. Mordecai points out that a crawler cannot use it to skip ahead. All it would do is let something out.

beats.headline: The water goes down the hole
beats.text: The plan was never a feral god. The Gate opens in the water quadrant, and a bubble's ocean, a load of timed charges and a feeding frenzy of sharks pour through it into Larracos's faction market. By Katia's math more than half of the inverted city is under water by the time the gate closes; only the upper levels, the NPC residences, are spared. Zev warns that the markets, the mercenaries and the Desperado Club's entrance bar are all down there. Juice Box flies for the gate and goes through with the water.

beats.headline: Still not drained
beats.text: Clarabelle, at the club door, says the level below the Hunting Grounds is still under water. Something keeps clogging the drains, and the sharks are not helping. The outworlders trapped on the Larracos level have the hotel and the main casino, so nobody is complaining much, but the weapons brokers who usually buy a pass up to trade with the hunters have not managed it once. They were trying to drain it before the floor ended. It does not look like they will.

beats.headline: The victory party, seen from the rubble
beats.text: A ninth-edition note from Rosetta in the Cookbook: when the viceroys pull out a last-minute victory, a portal opens, and the orcs, the viceroys, the operatics and the nagas step through together, laughing, off to a victory party in a nightclub on another floor. They drag unwilling NPCs with them, the librarian elves from the college among them. A crawler who tries to follow hits the portal like glass. The orc prince steps back into the smoldering remains of Larracos, lassoes him, and the rope cuts him in half on the way back through.

beats.headline: Home Team, based in Larracos
beats.text: One of the viewers' votes seats a tenth team, populated with NPCs and given the same protections as the other nine. It is designated Home Team, its base is the city of Larracos, and peace rules apply there effectively immediately, until the game starts. Its co-warlords are the NPCs Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand. An adjutant is to be assigned before the battles begin. It passes by fifty-two percent.

beats.headline: The crawl arrives inside it
beats.text: Crawlers come down into Larracos at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire. The armies that have spent eight floors drilling and drinking are allowed to fight one another at last, and the thing they are fighting over is underfoot: the castle at the bottom of the well.

beats.headline: Arief's tour
beats.text: War Leader Arief walks the group down from the college on level fifty through a city whose floodwater has fallen to its bottom three levels, still high enough to cover the castle. Juice Box has been waking its NPCs to the truth of what they are.

beats.headline: Zerzura
beats.text: The Sledge casts Zerzura and the city goes: Larracos and the shanty town outside its walls lifted whole and set down on the twelfth floor, NPC team and all. The outworlders who were standing in it are put out of the dungeon instead.

tagline.text: The city every hunter on this floor is sent to for thirty hours of grace before release, with at least one unguarded exit somewhere in it.
The capital of the sixth floor and the door the hunters come in through: a 1950s downtown with the stairwell down sitting in a park in its square.
The capital of the sixth floor, with a block of it blown to pieces and its Desperado Club entrance caved in.

beats.headline: The hunters' door
beats.text: The stairwell down stands in a quaint little park in the town square of the city every hunter on this floor has been gathered into. Bomo casts his teleport and puts Carl and Donut on its steps in the hours before the release.

beats.headline: The roof comes down
beats.text: Carl marks a drunk hunter with the Night Wyrm's ring, uses him as bait, kills him for his stat, and lines the street of pubs with barrel bombs. When they go, the Desperado Club's façade comes down on its entrance bar, and whoever was inside the club stays trapped there. He is shot to pieces getting clear of the town, and Miriam Dom and Prepotente carry him the rest of the way.

beats.headline: Mordecai's verdict
beats.text: The team says goodbye to Miriam and Prepotente at a small bugbear settlement. Mordecai is waiting to take Carl apart for what he did to the city, and Donut gets in first: yes, it was idiotic and suicidal, and no, she is not leaving him. Mordecai shuts his mouth and settles for pointing out that for all the noise, only a handful of hunters died.

beats.headline: A note on the door
beats.text: A second bomb is ready to walk back in when Carl finds a note pinned to a door: the hunters inside are proofed against explosives now, and the Hive is hunting him. It is signed. Vrah does that.

tagline.text: A dromedarian town out in the sand of a sealed bubble: a brothel town, city hall for dromedarians only, and changelings working Hump Street.
The town the Wasteland wants to bomb, and the reason Carl is riding a hijacked balloon up at it.

beats.headline: Down into the bubble
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia come down into the air quadrant of a sealed bubble and walk to one of the only two towns in it. Mordecai meets them there wearing a Skyfowl, which is what this floor has made of him. Donut takes the Glass Cannon class on the way in.

beats.headline: What is in the town hall
beats.text: Skarn lends Carl his telescope for a look out at the Wasteland, and explains why the gnomes riding it leave this town and the Bactrian village alone. It is not mercy. It is what both places keep in their town halls.

beats.headline: Regroup
beats.text: The party finds the other crawlers in town, among them Firas, Louis, and Langley's team of car salesmen who have taken up the bow. Carl, Donut and Katia set out for the Bactrian town without them, and a Thorny Devil and a Gnomish Drop Bear turn them back short of it, so they run for here instead.

beats.headline: The bombs never land
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia climb into the Vahana's basket and take it as it rises with Langley's team shooting from the ground. Carl puts missiles into the Wasteland's bombs before they can be dropped on the town. The Wasteland breaks apart and comes down. The castle it carried stays up.

tagline.text: A settlement across the river with a rule against nearly everything, dinosaurs emphatically included. Its new mayor named it after one.
A town with a rule against dinosaurs and a dinosaur named Big Tina working through its people.

beats.headline: A new mayor and a new name
beats.text: The settlement across the bridge keeps a long list of rules, and one of them is that Mongo does not come in. Donut kills the mayor, takes the office herself, and renames the place after the animal they would not admit.

beats.headline: The Recital quest
beats.text: Something has been coming out of the trees for the townspeople, and the job of looking into it lands on the party the same hour the new signage does. Mongo, for his part, runs off with Donut on his back, and Carl has to pull her out of the saddle in a clearing ringed by an all-female mongoliensis pack. Its leader does not want to fight him. Not exactly.

beats.headline: Back into town
beats.text: The group returns here after Clint's account of Scolopendra and the stolen thing that kept the high elves standing. The third and final sponsor signs as they cross its bridge. The Apothecary.

beats.headline: The attacks have a name
beats.text: The quest updates with the answer: the dinosaur eating the town is called Big Tina. Samantha's recon on the far shore turns up ursine bitten to pieces, one set of three-toed tracks and pink feathers everywhere, and Areson knows whose they are.

tagline.text: The Desperado Club's rival in the Over City: leather chairs, pipe smoke, old clerics, and no entry for anyone who drinks in the other place.
The Desperado Club's opposite number: leather chairs, pipe smoke, clerics, and a door that does not normally open for anyone who drinks in the other place.
Where the strongest temple on a floor almost always stands, so a worshipper of light can travel straight into it along a fairy's thread, unseen.

beats.headline: An acolyte's key
beats.text: Carl takes the vows of Emberus, and the benefits come with an asterisk: free access to Club Vanquisher, regardless of previous and current affiliations. Two quests come attached. Find Out Who Killed My Son, and Kill Hellik.

beats.headline: Pater Coal gives him a foot massage
beats.text: A high cleric walks Carl through the club to the Emberus High Temple, suppresses his slugpox, and tells him that Katia and Donut are each carrying something the god's quest needs. For the length of the sacrament, the AI is speaking through him.

beats.headline: He never went to the healer
beats.text: A look back at that visit: out of the temple and on the way to the healer, Carl stops Pater Coal and asks what happens if they do not go. Whatever he did instead, he has kept to himself.

beats.headline: Breaking into a country club
beats.text: Vinata and her guard mean to sit out the rest of the war in a temple inside the club, where nothing can reach them. So Katia, Carl, Prepotente and Samantha break in behind an unbroken line of wire running back to Li Na's clocktower, so her aura works inside, and Li Jun, Bautista and Zhang come in behind them to hold the doors and string the wire.

beats.headline: A bomb in the temple
beats.text: Katia and Prepotente drink Black Nimbus potions to get themselves thrown out of the temple. Then Carl casts Run, Little Günter, Run and drops a very big bomb in a very narrow room, and his immortality is all that holds him together. The blast throws him out of Khepri's temple and back in front of its portal, and Vinata, immortal herself, comes out with him, wrapped around him and crushing.

tagline.text: Where the top fifty crawlers are due to be sent for the high elves' party: contests, prizes, and a battle to finish it.
Queen Imogen's seat, the venue for the Butcher's Masquerade, and the prize written into the back half of a quest.
The last ground on the floor the brambles have not reached, which is why everybody is walking towards it.

beats.headline: The quest names the house
beats.text: Part two of Vengeance of the Daughter comes down: kill Signet's half-sister, Queen Imogen of the high elves, who leaves her chambers only for the yearly party the high elves throw for their elite, the same party the game's top players are invited to. The reward is the run of her castle, and the castle is said to hold the thing that turns Scolopendra's attack aside.

beats.headline: The brambles point at it
beats.text: Katia works the growth rate out. By the last day the creepers will have taken the whole floor, and the one place they finish is here. Katia's party starts moving that way, and Carl means to meet them there.

beats.headline: The map on the table
beats.text: The countdown to the Masquerade starts and the team goes over a map of the castle together, room by room. Donut's applications for the pet beauty contest and the talent show are both accepted.

beats.headline: The changelings have to be inside
beats.text: Carl and Donut blackmail their way onto the hunters' level of the Desperado Club to reach the changelings, and the message they carry is a map. The spell that can move the changelings works only on a town, the elves have razed every town in the forest but their own castle, and so the changelings have to be inside it.

beats.headline: The Sugar Cube
beats.text: Up close the castle is not stone. It is white wood, maybe bleached oak, carved all over with acorns the size of a fingernail as if the whole building were turned from one piece, and it is hot to the touch. Elle calls it the Sugar Cube and the name sticks. There used to be a moat; the queen had it drained because it smelled funny. A pencil-thin tower stands at each corner, and trolls fight the elves in the caves below.

beats.headline: Gone to the ninth floor
beats.text: When the Sledge's spell lands, the castle is simply gone, half-destroyed and set down somewhere on the ninth floor, and it has taken the subbasements with it. It has also taken Signet's tattoo warriors, the changelings, Kiwi as a very pregnant bear, and Tina, still a dinosaur. Everyone and everything else, mostly mantis nymphs, hangs frozen in a rough stacked cube over the pit where it stood.

beats.headline: The Lemig headquarters
beats.text: The castle landed in the Lemig Sortion's territory, and they made it their headquarters. In Queen Imogen's private ballroom near the top, their warlord waits for a summoned Carl, planning to leave him a vegetable and turn the spider loose on his own base. Instead the spider comes out in the ballroom. When it is over, Panford, the Lemig adjutant, tells Commander Stockade his throne room is destroyed and that it is being ruled an AI action. His general, Luke, killed by a fellow soldier under her control, is among the dead.

tagline.text: Where a glass case in the inventory was forged, by its own description: the mysterious fifteenth level of the dungeon.
Half of a bomb, by its own description: an overloaded soul crystal inside a case forged in its fires.
Where the demons come from, and where, evicted by an excess of death, they may only go back by dragging an extra soul down with them.
It has princes. One of them is on this floor, in the body of a giant snake.

beats.headline: A part in a bomb
beats.text: The word arrives the way most of the dungeon's cosmology does: buried in an item description. A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is half of what makes an explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god. The case's own description says it was forged in the fires of Sheol, the mysterious fifteenth level of the World Dungeon, and nobody asks what that means.

beats.headline: Bricks in the cab
beats.text: The box at the back of the Nightmare Express's cab holds about fifty Sheol Bricks. The item description promises not to say where they come from, then admits it: it is a baby corpse. The stoker's own description has the arithmetic. A Lesser Demon's labour runs about sixty days and delivers fifteen to eighteen thousand young, one in ten thousand viable; the rest harden into fuel that burns long and hot. Carl drops the first brick and wipes his hand on his cloak. Then he takes the whole box into his inventory.

beats.headline: The Demon Eviction opens the door
beats.text: So much dies on the eighth floor at once that the dungeon declares a Demon Eviction, and the eviction runs in one direction: out of Sheol and onto the floor, looking for bodies to inhabit. The realm has been adjacent this whole time, waiting on a body count.

beats.headline: Its fire, released by a benefit
beats.text: Carl burns his own health down inside Samantha's acidic neck, too slowly to beat the timer. It goes on dropping afterwards, and once he is under five percent his Martyr's Path benefit engulfs every step he has taken outside in flame, and with his fire still enhanced, that flame is Sheol fire. The realm's fire is a resource now, one a crawler can spend without ever having gone there.

beats.headline: One of six powers in the dungeon
beats.text: The AI sets out who is actually fighting for control down here, and there are six groups. Crawlers. Standard NPCs. Gods. Sapient mobs. The demons of Sheol. And one more it does not name in the same breath as the others.

beats.headline: The floor that segregated itself
beats.text: Laying out the road to the exit, the AI says the fifteenth floor can probably be skipped. Sheol has segregated itself out, and the dungeon programming is pretending it sits outside the playing field, like the thirteenth floor in some hotels. The AI admits it does not know what is going on down there. Someone, it says, should probably check on that.

beats.headline: A front of its own
beats.text: Louis drops through the casino's portal expecting the Pineapple Cabaret and lands in Sheol instead: a hot cave on the fifteenth floor, outside the playing field without a registered pass. Its people separated themselves from the code in time to miss the first Scolopendra attack. A demon called Forkith gives Louis a leech that filters a crawler's blood so he can survive the heat. They need soldiers on a different front, he says, and they have been waiting a very long time to move.

tagline.text: Station 10, which the engineer says is really just the yard: where he finds himself back on the platform with no memory of the trip.
Station ten on the tangle, through the Station Repair portal: a high-fenced yard of engine cars, and thousands of zombies penned in with them.

beats.headline: The switch nobody is meant to take
beats.text: The named trains run their loops until they reach a set of three switches, and only one of them leads here. Getting to it means reading the network, or else noticing that the souvenir conductor hat handed out at the start of the floor is one of the keys, which is the sort of joke the fourth floor keeps making.

beats.headline: A yard given up to ghouls
beats.text: Station and Repair Hub E is not coping. The DTs have been turning mobs into Festering Ghouls born knowing how to get here, and thousands have arrived, pushing the fence back and forth. According to Widget, someone cheaped out combining two systems: the ghouls were meant to be caged and conveyed onward, the cages broke, and too many came at once. The staff are about to abandon the yard for Yard A. Then a section of the great wall collapses, and the ghouls surge out of the enclosure toward the conductor staging area beyond it.

tagline.text: The Dirigible Gnomes' castle in the sky, as the wheel names it: the Wasteland Fortress. Storm it, and the level is passed.
A gnomish dreadnought that is also a castle and also somebody’s home, floating over the air quadrant with the way down sitting inside it.

beats.headline: The castle is the aircraft
beats.text: The flying home of the dirigible gnomes and a heavily armed military platform, and there is no seam between the two. It holds the air quadrant of the bubble, and the stairs down sit inside it, which settles what anyone wanting to leave the floor is going to have to do about it.

beats.headline: Sky garden, renamed dreadnaught
beats.text: The Vahana, the black-and-gold striped Gnomish Legate Balloon that comes down to parley, is perhaps the oldest vehicle left aboard the Wasteland, and its description tells the gnomes' side. They once took to the skies hoping to stay out of this world's wars as neutral peacekeepers, and a Legate balloon on the horizon meant ambassadors and perhaps peace. Then winged predators came through a mysterious portal and would share the sky with nobody. The balloons were mostly dismantled and sewn into the settlements' defences, and the flying communities changed their name from sky garden to dreadnaught.

beats.headline: The air quadrant liberated
beats.text: The last piece of the Wasteland comes down in a hurry and stops just short. With Denise dead in the kitchen's garbage disposal, the Commandant's quarters count as occupied, and a bubble notification congratulates crawlers Princess Donut and Carl on taking the throne room. The Air Quadrant is liberated, and every crawler who started there may now travel freely into the other quadrants. Then the house bumps gently onto the ground.

tagline.text: One of the lit doors in the club: the strip club and brothel for those who prefer dudes. Mordecai's advice is not to go in.
The ground-floor strip club of the Desperado Club, and by some distance the least exclusive of the three.

beats.headline: First floor of the club, and it shows
beats.text: The entrance sits off the Desperado Club’s top floor, and the System admits there is a hierarchy: the deeper the level, the better the performers, at least in theory. It is staffed, it is loud, and it smells of male sweat, grease and cheap cologne.

entities.name: Pandinus
entities.role: Pazuzu town · fifth floor, land quadrant

tagline.text: A pazuzu town on the land quadrant, all scorpion tails and post-apocalyptic leather, and the only place a quarter turn around the bowl that would take the party in.
The scorpion town on the land quadrant where the party drinks, recruits, and comes out of the Gate of the Feral Gods with a wall of seawater behind them.

beats.headline: A town that would take them in
beats.text: After the sandcastle the party had to track a quarter turn around the land quadrant before any town would let them in. This one did. Its people are pazuzu, half human and half scorpion, built like centaurs and dressed as though the world already ended: punk leather, tassels, goggles, chains and dreadlocks, all bound for a Mad Max convention. Louis and Firas went off to sleep, Louis grumbling about the drink. Once Mordecai walked off, Carl's question about the place was whether it had a Desperado Club.

beats.headline: The Death Stalker
beats.text: Smaller than Hump Town, with several inns and taverns. No Desperado Club, but a Club Vanquisher, currently closed for cleansing after Prepotente set his hellspawn goat loose in the main lounge over Miriam Dom's revoked membership. So the party met at The Death Stalker: a few tables, a bar and, inexplicably, a gelato cart with about twenty flavours. Donut talked the pazuzu down from two gold to one for a bowl of raspberry. Two crawlers from the water quadrant joined them at the table.

beats.headline: A wall of water
beats.text: Carl dialled the Gate of the Feral Gods to a spot just outside town, and he, Katia and Tran splashed out onto the beach inside a wall of seawater. The portal was open three or four seconds. That was enough to topple the metal wall, knock over a guard tower and put a chunk of metal through one pazuzu's front door like a javelin. Any longer and the town would have gone the way of the sandcastle. They ran for the nearest inn, past a staring bartender.

beats.headline: Feral pazuzu out of the sand
beats.text: Night, a rising storm, waves slapping the pub windows, and the pazuzu barkeep huddled behind his bar pointing outside with a shaking hand. When the giant dog jumped, a stone statue off the necropolis crushed a pazuzu hut two hundred feet away. Then a wave of feral pazuzu came up through the sand. Carl caught one stinger in his hand, immune to the venom but not to the hole, tore off the tip, and stabbed its owner in the neck with it.

tagline.text: Fort Freedom: the naiads' former river palace, where the leaders of the Naiad Confederacy are holed up, and the first target of Signet's revenge.
Fort Freedom, the naiad castle, retaken by Tsarina Signet. Barely a fight: the confederates had stopped ruling long ago and had lost their own throne room to an eryops.

beats.headline: Part one of two
beats.text: The Vengeance of the Daughter, part one of two. Tsarina Signet, exiled half-daughter of the naiads, has come home to a kingdom marred by infighting and a sloppy revolution that cut off the head of the government and left the body flailing. The current leaders of the Naiad Confederacy are holed up in the former river palace, now dubbed Fort Freedom. Assault it, avenge her mother's assassination, and survivors follow your orders twenty percent more willingly. The name is doing a lot of work.

beats.headline: A castle mostly underwater
beats.text: Night in the forest, heading north to join Signet's assault team at one of the old trees before approaching the river. Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut have only a minor role tonight; Signet is plainly saving them for part two. That suits the cat, because the castle is mostly submerged, and she has reiterated her position on going underwater several times. Carl is more concerned with part two, and with which programme gets to own its climax.

beats.headline: Traps all the way down
beats.text: From the treeline, Fort Freedom glitters in the dark. The river is a mile and a half wide here. The naiads have cleared the long, muddy slope so nothing can approach unseen, and one stone-paved trail runs down to an archway at the water. The slope lights up with traps: alarms, summoning traps, silent alarms along the walkway. Inside, the usurpers occupy the castle and neither maintain it nor rule. They were so obsessed with being free that they forgot what governing involves.

beats.headline: The front door is the decoy
beats.text: The plan is child's play because the defence is a joke. An alarm goes off at the front, the poorly trained guards run toward it, and Signet's amphibious team comes in the undefended rear, straight to the throne room, where the confederacy's leaders are conveniently hiding. Samantha is given a long line to deliver if captured, announcing herself as Psamathe. Signet walks in with the water shying away from her. Then the bodies start surfacing: naiads, paper soldiers, and what is probably a bush elf, ripped in half.

beats.headline: An eryops on the throne
beats.text: Whatever holds the throne room is a lightning-shooting river monster, and Samantha has her teeth in it. Claude Sludgington the Fourth, Eryops Gigantis, arrives beside Crawler Carl at truck size. His history: short of gold, because they would not tax anyone yet still owed tithes to the high elves, the confederates threw a fundraiser ball at fifty gold a head. Nobody came. The citizens were starving and eating anyone near the water. Claude did come, and the guards let him in.

beats.headline: Barely a fight
beats.text: Premature Questjaculation: a quest is beaten before it can even be handed out, so the reward is nothing. Tsarina Signet takes the castle. Plenty of guards, an algae infestation, confederates who stopped attempting to rule ages ago, a throne room surrendered to an eryops, a kingdom in shambles. It would have fallen on its own within months. Part one completes. Part two names the true culprit: the high elves, and Queen Imogen.

tagline.text: Shanty Town: a ring around Larracos, named in the ceasefire warning as the one place the ban on entering the city does not reach.
A ring of hovels around the mouth of Larracos that nobody actually built, bigger than any season's before, with food markets, temples, and a mayor who keeps getting killed.
The ring around Larracos, pink on the map now: controlled by the Princess Posse, bought from Ferdinand with a bowler hat.
Flattened by the passage of two gods, most of its towers never used.
Handed back to the NPCs, joined to Larracos, and carried away with it to the twelfth floor.

beats.headline: An exception in the fine print
beats.text: The warning about the ceasefire is mostly bad news. When it expires, only members of the defending team may remain within the city of Larracos, and that restriction holds until certain conditions are met. Then one line more: the restriction does not apply to the Shanty Town ring. Ten teams remain, and every one of them has just been told there is a ring around the city where they are allowed to stand.

beats.headline: Hovels nobody built
beats.text: There is usually a shanty town. Never one like this. It appeared soon after the flooding, supposedly built by displaced NPCs, except that nobody built it: the hovels simply sprang up, a full ring round the top entrance of Larracos, large enough to count as a settlement. It has new shops and new NPCs, food markets and temples, and one hard-to-find Club Vanquisher entrance, but no weapons or mercenary markets. Its mayors keep dying. The gnoll Theora lost a single combat to a cheat. The current mayor, Juice Box says, pained, is someone else.

beats.headline: Mayor, for a bowler hat
beats.text: Crawler Carl wanted to be mayor of Shanty Town, and the mayor was Ferdinand. The deal: Ferdinand transferred the mayorship, the jewel on his necklace went away, and he got a bowler hat to wear until they trade it back for his turban in a day or so. Juice Box was on board. Carl's reasoning, on the walk back: if the bad guys can freely enter Shanty Town once the truce breaks, it is a liability, and it has a defence system of its own.

beats.headline: Pink on the map
beats.text: On the hologram of the floor a tiny ring around Larracos blinks and turns pink: Shanty Town, controlled by the Princess Posse. Baroness Victory calls it a smart trade. The shanty town is usually small and does not form until the fighting starts and the NPCs flee, but this one circles the whole city, giving the NPCs another layer of security, and the Posse holds it. Li Na asks, the moment she is recruited, that her squad build the defences in and around it.

beats.headline: No throne room
beats.text: The 107th White Dragons are parked in the makeshift town, and it worries Crawler Carl: it is shaped like a donut and can be attacked from nearly any angle. Nobody has tried yet. Entering Shanty Town exposes an attacker to the Larracos defence system, and the town's rules are different. There is no throne room. The only way to take it is to kill Carl. Li Na's battalion, meanwhile, is bankrupting the Posse's coffers building its defences.

beats.headline: The third front
beats.text: The round border of Shanty Town is now the Posse's third front. Juice Box, stingy with support until now, lends ground troops to hold it: Semeru dwarves and ordinary citizens of Larracos, mixed in with Li Na's 107th White Dragon Urban Defense battalion in a ring around the lip of the city. None of the enemy may enter Larracos until four teams remain, but Shanty Town itself is exposed. At the base of the Nest tower, Crawler Donut asks whether it is too late to paint it another colour.

beats.headline: Frozen where they stood
beats.text: Eris casts Bear Witness, and most of Shanty Town is caught. Li Na reports: those inside structures are fine, she and Li Jun among them, but Zhang was outside. Anyone who was once a tattoo is unaffected, and so are the sluggalos. Everyone else is a frozen witness, and across the floor the frozen witnesses rise into the air and disappear.

beats.headline: Trampled by two gods
beats.text: The fight between the gods passes through the other side of Shanty Town, and then it is simply gone. Most of the defensive towers the Posse paid for, and never really got to use, are trampled. The Nest tower and Li Na's abandoned synergy towers still stand, drawing a lot of fire. Every other building is flattened.

beats.headline: Ceded back to the NPCs
beats.text: Clean-up is shared: NPCs, won-over mercenaries, veterans and crawlers repairing towers side by side, with Ferdinand directing the Nest tower. Mordecai thinks Shanty Town can be adjoined to Larracos. It first has to be ceded back to the NPCs, and the Posse has already done it. Meanwhile the top defensive ring of the city is being readied, towers repaired and their spells changed out.

beats.headline: Inside the glow
beats.text: Rosetta, on the chat: it worked. Shanty Town is included in the glow, and the two towns have been combined. The entire funnel city of Larracos, Shanty Town with it, is about to be transferred to the twelfth floor as the Sledge casts. Rosetta is moving to the saferoom with Tipid and the others, and she has Samantha with her.

entities.name: The Pineapple Cabaret
entities.role: Hidden pocket dimension · behind the seventeenth floor

tagline.text: The Pineapple Cabaret. One of four places the AI offers to send a banished orc princess, and only the backstage part of it. She chooses elsewhere.
The Pineapple Cabaret. A pocket dimension behind the seventeenth floor, built by two forgotten former crawlers as a refuge for mobs and NPCs. No worshipper of a god may enter.
The Pineapple Cabaret. Two hundred and twenty-seven crawlers have gone through by cleaner bot, with Li Na ahead of them. A cactus with one flower says it is safe.

beats.headline: Backstage, if you please
beats.text: The AI, wearing Growler Gary, offers Princess Formidable four choices after her attempt on the fail-safe: death, the Scolopendra Club, the Cabaret backstage, or Earth's surface. Ten seconds. She asks what the hells the cabaret is. The Pineapple Cabaret, it says, though backstage at it, not the cabaret itself, and not a bad choice. Tick tock. She picks the surface and teleports away with a crack. The AI hopes she knows how to swim.

beats.headline: A note under a dirty drawing
beats.text: A blank invoice from C&W&U, a shop that opens after the third heat, carries a crude drawing for the gremlins and, legible only to Crawler Carl's Escape Plan skill, a message from Akuma: kill two teams next heat, visit the shop and ask for top-shelf upgrades, we want the same thing. I can smuggle friends to the Pineapple Cabaret. We can escape this chaos. Come alone. Carl has heard the name exactly once, when the AI offered it to an orc princess as a place of banishment. It is not in the Cookbook.

beats.headline: Eris vouches for the door
beats.text: Eris, recruiting, tells Crawler Carl to make nice with Akuma and his head-exploding mages: he really does have a way to crack open the Pineapple Cabaret. Akuma thinks it is his exit ticket, and it is much more than that. The war mages probably turn on the crawlers at the end, she says, but not right away; they need each other. She does not care what happens to them as long as the path to the Cabaret is open, because it is a way for some of Carl's friends to escape.

beats.headline: What it is, under questioning
beats.text: Akuma, questioned in considerable pain, explains. Many seasons ago two indentured former crawlers asked a showrunner for the job of building the seventeenth floor. The showrunner agreed, was murdered soon after, and never transferred the paperwork, so the two were forgotten: ghosts in the system, rebuilding the floor every season unsupervised. The floor is a front. Attached to it is the only entrance to a pocket dimension they built as an oasis, where mobs and NPCs can escape the dungeon for good. They gave up any chance of leaving to make it. That is the Pineapple Cabaret.

beats.headline: Nobody who worships a god
beats.text: The terms. The Cabaret is not a floor but a separate dimension, like the Nothing, and the rules allow crawlers into it; anyone inside when a floor collapses counts as lost, not killed. With the Gate broken there are two possible ways in: the casinos at the Desperado Club, or something involving the shop interface, which was Herot's idea. And nobody who worships a god may enter. It would bring a smite, and the Cabaret cannot risk being drawn into the Ascendency battles. That rules out Crawler Carl, and most of his friends.

beats.headline: A standing order for cleaner bots
beats.text: Mordecai reports that the test worked, on Samantha and then on some sluggalos. The explanation for the missing cleaner bots is Herot, inside the Cabaret with limited powers and a shop interface and a standing order to buy every one that appears. Menerva runs the NPCs building the Backstage Death Maze on the seventeenth floor. The Cabaret itself is overrun, by ogres from a binned plotline, a shadow mimic infestation and more, and the war mages want help clearing it. The casino plan looks like a bust. Li Na, dying of poison, is to go first, if she can be talked into it.

beats.headline: One flower means come
beats.text: Li Na's passage is reported by a dread cactus that stays with Crawler Carl. If it crumbles to dust, she died inside the dungeon. If its glow fails slowly over several days, she is trapped in the cleaner bot's storage and never released. If she reaches the Pineapple Cabaret and believes it safe for others to follow, she can make a single flower bloom on top. Alive but unsafe is three flowers. Crawler Donut repeats it back to be sure.

beats.headline: Two hundred and twenty-seven
beats.text: It goes smoothly. Crawler Carl's cleaner bot fits forty people; Bobby Montague's fits a hundred and five. Two hundred and twenty-seven crawlers go to the Pineapple Cabaret, not counting Li Na, and among them are Zhang, Tran, Daniel, Archie and Randall 3. Every cleaner bot for sale is bought immediately. Mordecai reports the cactus steady, glowing, with a single bloom. Each of the departed now has a small potted plant under glass in the guildhall, and Crawler Donut names it the Garden of Deliverance.

beats.headline: The back door, contested
beats.text: The shadow mimic Mitch, cornered, admits they needed some of the crawlers for the Cabaret: the war mages, the ogres and something called Cock-A-Doodle-Do all vie for control of the dungeon's back door. For Louis and others, the plan was a jump from the casino to a holding area, where Herot, inside the Pineapple Cabaret, pulls them out. Louis jumps and wakes in Sheol instead. The demon who greets him there says the Pineapple Cabaret has more than enough hands to protect it.

tagline.text: Hungry Eyes Village. A dot on the GPS beside the finish line, and a spread of colourful lights at the far end of a cave.
Hungry Eyes. A neon, 1980s-cyberpunk town behind the racers' cul-de-sacs: bars, temples, street food. Safe room rules stop at the main square; poisoning rules stop everywhere.
Hungry Eyes. The main square where two hundred crawlers bound for the Pineapple Cabaret gathered to say goodbye before a heat.

beats.headline: Lights at the end of the cave
beats.text: End of the first heat. The racers come out of the cave, and two dots appear on the GPS, labelled Hungry Eyes Village and Finish Line, as a spread of colourful lights shows up in the distance. Would you look at that, says Crawler Carl, as the town comes into view. Crawler Donut misses it entirely. She is absorbed in Elle's running report on an awkward meeting with a fan who wants a giant pillow with Elle on it signed.

beats.headline: A bar for hiring help
beats.text: Hedy, the court's engineer, sets out the crew rules: up to three mercenaries each heat, previously hired ones allowed under the same rules, and a bar out in Hungry Eyes where they can be hired. She reckons the best ones have already been snatched, the court having taken its sweet time getting here. Crawler Donut rules out Samantha as crew for any race whatsoever, citing an attention span like a Cornish Rex. Crawler Carl raises no objection.

beats.headline: The team roundabout cul-de-sac
beats.text: Through the garage door is the court's team roundabout, officially part of Hungry Eyes: an asphalt cul-de-sac under a red sun, ringed by nine garage doors, eight numbered and one painted with a runny red skull. Manicured grass, tall trees, the smell of cut lawn. The court's door carries a big 7. A truck can leave the garage and go nowhere, and a narrow path leads to a see-through portal onto a neon settlement. The bugbears of team Free Love are out in lawn chairs with peach beer. Safe room rules apply.

beats.headline: Neon, and eat at your own risk
beats.text: The vendor village proper. Safe room rules do not apply in the main square, and poisoning rules do not apply anywhere. Where most towns in the dungeon run faux-medieval, this one is a 1980s cyberpunk fever dream in pink, teal and purple, mostly gremlins, a few Draconians. Flashing temples, one of them a Club Vanquisher entrance Crawler Carl is banned from. An unsigned storefront, C&W&U, grand opening soon. A bar called the Hairpin, with the Desperado Club entrance in the back, and the Lollipop next door.

beats.headline: Goodbye in the main square
beats.text: Volunteers for the assault on the Pineapple Cabaret gather in the commons of Hungry Eyes, where Tran and Zhang chase off the NPCs and set up tables, and Linus's goodbye party joins them because he is barred from town between the sixth and seventh heats. Before the heat, all two hundred crawlers bound for the transfer, and several of their friends, fill the main square: too many for the guild's common room, so the farewell happens here, and then there is a race to run.

beats.headline: The Outreach Guild opens
beats.text: A system message: the Outreach Guild is now available in Hungry Eyes. Crawler Donut declines to visit. Before the final heat, crawlers queue along the street to enter it, and Prepotente walks the line collecting last-minute items from their inventories as they go in. So far nobody who has entered has come back out. Crawler Carl finds that somewhat encouraging, since it suggests the deals on offer inside are at least decent, and is tempted to join the queue just to talk to Quasar.

tagline.text: A name in the red line's announcements: at transfer station 83, one may access the yellow line and the Nightmare Express.
A named train on a figure-eight loop, once every hour and a half. Five stops, and one of them, station 436, is one higher than the end of the line.
A jet-black steam engine hauling forty cars of caged monsters, until Carl stole it. Its fire is kept by a lesser demon who gives birth in the firebox.
Carl's stolen train. It carried him to the abyss, into the yard and down the employee line, ferried the Daughters, and made its last run through a portal loaded to explode.

beats.headline: Next stop, transfer station 83
beats.text: The first mention is a train announcer's patter. Aboard the red line, with a service plate that wants a Red Line Engineer's Key and monsters in the next car, the loudspeaker crackles: coming up on Mora station number 82, home to the Psycho Stickers. Watch out for those guys. Next stop is transfer station number 83, where one may access the yellow line and the Nightmare Express. After that, Rusalka station 84. Thank you for riding the red line. Then the door starts to slide.

beats.headline: A train called that
beats.text: Station 83's small circular hall has two more stairwells, one to the yellow line and one to the Nightmare Express. Over dinner Carl notes that the stairwells are all at lower numbers. Donut bets the lines without colour names are the way back, and says they should ride the Nightmare line to see where it goes. She is probably right. Carl does not like the idea of immediately jumping onto a train called The Nightmare Express. Mordecai's own station, in his season, had a big one called the Misery.

beats.headline: A figure eight
beats.text: They miss it while shopping; it only comes every hour and a half. The platform says enough. Wider tracks, no electrified third rail, a platform twice as long as the red line's. The route map is a figure eight with five stops: four transit stations, and at the very top, station 436. Station 83, yellow and red; station 283, mauve and purple; 436; 283 again, green and yellow; a different 83, tangerine and plum. They weren't kidding, Carl says, when they named this thing the Iron Tangle.

beats.headline: Not until the shell resets
beats.text: Katia draws the route on a giant sheet of paper. The Nightmare Express stops two stations down on the Mauve line, and since it runs all the way up to 436, one higher than the supposed end of the line, it can show them the very end in hours instead of days. Aboard the Dismemberment Limited, with a war mage and his fleshers at the door, Carl adds a condition. They are not boarding the Nightmare until his Protective Shell is ready again.

beats.headline: Forty cars and no way in
beats.text: At station 283 it eases in: an old-school steam engine painted jet black, a wedge-shaped cowcatcher, about forty cars. Most are open-topped livestock cars caged to the ceiling with chain link, and in them massive things scrabble to get out: tentacles, claws and fire, one car full of seawater and spikes. The only ways aboard are a caboose and a passenger car behind the engine marked exit only. The train takes a minute and a half to leave. Protective Shell lasts twenty seconds.

beats.headline: Hit by the Nightmare
beats.text: So Carl walks up the tunnel with Donut on his shoulder, casts Protective Shell as the train bears down, and Puddle Jumper carries them a quarter-mile down the track. Every monster aboard slams into the wall of the spell. The train speeds up. It catches Carl as he leaps for the platform: the cowcatcher, then the front of the engine, his invulnerable foot taking the hit. He climbs the boiler, punches in the cab window and finds two dead engineers, and gauges climbing toward a train-sized grenade.

beats.headline: A stolen goddamned train
beats.text: A face in the firebox window talks him down: Fire Brandy, the Fire(wo)man, who says the engineer and a war mage went splat and walks him through the valves until the bomb warning goes away, then the throttle and the two-control brakes. In the gore of the cab Carl finds a Steam Engineer's Key, good for all four hundred steam trains of the Tangle. The shell killed every monster aboard, three neighborhood bosses among them. The cars behind are flatbeds now. Carl has stolen a goddamned train.

beats.headline: Up to 436
beats.text: Past a switching station, with its Station Repair portal and a track called Recycle, the train reaches Abyss Station, 436. A steep fire-escape stair climbs to a catwalk inside a burning pit of portals, where engineless colored-line trains burst through and tumble onto thousands of crashed cars below. Carl comes back down with the answer, the conductor's hat, and sends it to everyone he knows. The train is still there, boiler chugging on standby. About two hours after that it is back at 283 for Katia.

beats.headline: First the Raven Blade, now the Nightmare
beats.text: Through the Station Repair portal the whole train makes it, into Station and Repair Hub E: a yard at least a mile deep, lit by spotlights, and thousands of festering ghouls penned inside its fence. A furious creature comes out to tell them the station is closed. First the Raven Blade Unlimited, and now the Nightmare? There is a ghoul infestation, and nobody is getting a resupply. Donut, sent to find the gate controls, opens the gate by accident.

beats.headline: A parade float
beats.text: The Nightmare waits where they left it on the dark employee line, idling, while the ghouls leave the track alone. Hekla's team wants to ride. There is no room in the cab, so Carl, Donut and Katia climb in while Hekla, Eva and a few others stand on the back platform, the rest clutching the railings on either side of the boiler, and small fairy-like daughters perch on the platform above the cowcatcher. It looks, Carl thinks, like a parade float.

beats.headline: Parked at sixty
beats.text: Its last job was ferrying Brynhild's Daughters to station sixty, and it is still parked there, a few stations down the employee line. Fire Brandy is still aboard and has turned away a pair of dwarven engineers who climbed in through the broken window: there is nowhere to go, you fool. Mordecai, told about the capture by Donut, assumes Carl thought that was a glorious idea too. Carl says it was a dumb idea. The new one is better. Though it's funny Mordecai mentions the Nightmare.

beats.headline: Its last run
beats.text: Tizquick the dwarf helps drive it down to the trainyard, where the portal cart waits on the employee track, and Carl explains the plan to Elle: send the Nightmare into the abyss loaded to explode, and knock out the ghoul system. Fire Brandy and Tizquick tell him they are staying aboard. He has a few more explosive satchels to place at the back. The train backs up to the edge of the yard, whistles twice, and speeds toward the portal. Afterwards Bautista reports that they felt the generator explode.

beats.headline: The name, painted on a plane
beats.text: On the fifth floor, Carl fills a gnomish biplane with a quarter tank of fuel for a run at the castle in the sky. A rabid koala is painted on its nose, and above it, in Syndicate standard, the plane's name: Death Trap, with four bombs painted after the tag. Carl covers it with a can of spray paint and writes Nightmare II on the side. Donut objects, but only half-heartedly.
